title: Security Hardening Checklist knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Security Hardening Checklist”?
options: Database security combines identity, least-privilege access, encrypted connections, safe query construction, and reviewable operations. Do not embed credentials in source code or grant an application more authority than it needs.
It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.
questions.answer_key: Database security combines identity, least-privilege access, encrypted connections, safe query construction, and reviewable operations. Do not embed credentials in source code or grant an application more authority than it needs.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: Database security combines identity, least-privilege access, encrypted connections, safe query construction, and reviewable operations. Do not embed credentials in source code or grant an application more authority than it needs.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Security Hardening Checklist” safely?
options: Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Propose a least-privilege role and a credential-safe connection, then explain how you would verify the effective permissions.
questions.answer_key: Propose a least-privilege role and a credential-safe connection, then explain how you would verify the effective permissions.
questions.explanation: Propose a least-privilege role and a credential-safe connection, then explain how you would verify the effective permissions. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Security Hardening Checklist”, what should be verified?
options: Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation. The CodeLeaf editor displays reference output only; real behavior depends on the selected server/runtime.
